standard: NFPA 13 (2019 edition) - Table 7.2.2.1, Sprinkler Discharge Characteristics Identification
note: Nominal K-factors as published. The calculator always takes K from the caller's input rather than this table, which exists to populate a dropdown: a listed sprinkler's actual K comes from its data sheet and need only fall inside the published range. kFactorRangeMinGpm/MaxGpm are that allowed range; percentOfK56Discharge is the table's discharge comparison against a K-5.6 head; threadType is the published thread, NOT an orifice size.
metricColumnNote: CHALLENGED AND UPHELD. A 2016-edition copy of this table (numbered 6.2.3.1 there) gave nominalKLpmBar as 28, 61 and 81 for K=1.9, 4.2 and 5.6, against the 27, 60 and 80 stored here. The stored column is the one that holds up: it equals round(K x 14.29) on twelve of the thirteen rows, and the three disputed cells are exactly the three where that pattern picks our value. The only row where neither fits the pattern is K=8.0 (14.29 gives 114.3, published as 115), and both copies agree on 115 there, so that is the standard's own rounding rather than an error on either side. The same copy also carried two provable transcription errors in other tables, so its three outliers here are read as the same kind of slip. No values changed.
dryTypeNote: Per the table's own note, these nominal K-factors are used for sprinkler SELECTION. Dry-type sprinklers use an adjusted K-factor for hydraulic calculation purposes (see 27.2.4.10.3). This application does not apply that adjustment - a caller calculating a dry-type sprinkler must pass the adjusted K.
